case_name: Haryana State Electricity Board & Anr v Gulshan Lal & Ors.
facts: The Haryana State Electricity Board & Anr v Gulshan Lal & Ors. case was heard by the Supreme Court of India.
Anil Kapoor and others filed a suit against the Haryana State Electricity Board, claiming equal pay for equal work.
Gulshan Lal and Others also filed a suit, praying for declaration and mandatory injunction.
Kashmir Singh and Others filed a suit, seeking higher grades and arrears of such higher grade, pay scales from the date of anomalies/ discrimination.
issues: Whether the doctrine of 'equal pay for equal work' applies to the case.
Whether the respondents are entitled to higher pay scales as claimed.
Whether the respondents have been doing the same nature of job which eleven other co-employees had been doing.
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners argued that they were senior to Anil Kapoor and Others, and therefore should receive higher pay scales.
They also argued that they were supervisors while the Technicians were working under their control and supervision.
respondent_arguments: The respondents argued that they had been doing the same nature of job which eleven other co-employees had been doing, and therefore should receive equal pay for equal work.
court_reasoning: The court held that the petitioners' claim was based on the doctrine of 'equal pay for equal work', but failed to establish any foundational fact as regards basis of their entitlement.
The court also noted that the respondents had been appointed after 1.01.1986, and therefore could not have claimed parity with Anil Kapoor.
holding: The court dismissed the petitioners' appeal, upholding the decision of the High Court in Anil Kapoor's RSA No. 800 of 1992.
The court also directed that the respondents be given the benefits as laid in Annexure P-3 within a period of six months from the date a certified copy of this order is received by the respondents.
